# Offline session parity fixtures

From the worktree root, run `just stage-parity` after building `corral-next` and `corrald-next` in `target/debug` and installing the Pi package dependencies. It prints the workspace, daemon socket, browser listener and pairing command, plus an open `parity-ready` build and its transcript path. Both the seed and any sessions started by the daemon use the real Pi host with `real-provider.json` in place of the model provider.

To record `tools.jsonl`, set `workspace` to the printed workspace and launch from `apps/corral-app`:

```sh
XDG_STATE_HOME="$workspace/app-state" XDG_DATA_HOME="$workspace/app-data" \
  CORRAL_SOCKET="$workspace/.corral-next/daemon.sock" nsh run --target tui --port 8891
```

Enroll this scratch client from Settings › Connection, or pair a browser in a private profile using the printed command. Open `parity-ready`, send `list the files` and wait for it to settle, then send `parity scenario`. Wait for the two child reports and the background job, answer **Parity (recommended)** in the question card, and wait for the edit, commit and final reply. Stop the job if desired. Before stopping staging, copy the printed transcript verbatim to `packages/corral-pi/test/fixtures/sessions/tools.jsonl`. The file is generated by the scripted run, never authored or edited by hand.

Replay the recording with `just stage-parity-fake test/fixtures/sessions/tools.json` (after recording it). Without a recording, `just stage-parity-fake` holds verification; substitute `test/fixtures/sessions/failed-gate.json`, `large.json`, or `older.json` (each under `test/fixtures/sessions/`) for a failed gate, 40 children and 300 queued inputs, or an unregistered `jobs` method. Paths passed to the recipe are relative to `packages/corral-pi` unless absolute. Fake state is frozen: reads return scripted data; controls do not run tools or advance the scenario.

For other offline recordings or binary locations, run `bun --no-env-file test/support/stage.ts --provider-script /path/to/steps.json --daemon /path/to/corrald-next --engine /path/to/corral-next` from `packages/corral-pi`. The binary flags can also be set via `CORRALD_NEXT_BIN` and `CORRAL_NEXT_BIN`. Use `--listen` and `--origin` for other fixed local ports. Ctrl-C stops staging and deletes the scratch workspace.
